questions.question: Which file provides the Next.js middleware for this app, and what is its exported handler function named?
questions.ground_truth: src/proxy.ts, exporting `async function proxy(request)` (Next 16 renamed the middleware.ts convention to proxy.ts).
questions.verify_output:
76:export async function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
122:export const config = {
questions.why_it_matters: An agent looking for middleware.ts or writing an exported `middleware` function will silently create a second, dead routing file that never runs.

questions.question: How many top-level route groups exist under src/app, and what are they?
questions.ground_truth: 4: (admin), (courier), (customer), (marketing).
questions.verify_output:
src/app/(admin)
src/app/(courier)
src/app/(customer)
src/app/(marketing)
questions.why_it_matters: Placing a new page in the wrong group changes which layout/auth wrapper it inherits, silently breaking role scoping.

questions.question: Does the POST handler at src/app/enter/[role]/route.ts (a passwordless role-login doorway) function in a production build?
questions.ground_truth: No — it checks NODE_ENV==='production' and redirects to /login instead, so the doorway is dev/staging-only by construction.
questions.why_it_matters: An agent could assume this passwordless login path is reachable in prod and either rely on it or flag it as a live vulnerability when it's actually inert there.

questions.question: Is there an INSERT RLS policy on delivery_status_events that lets any client role write to it directly?
questions.ground_truth: No — every occurrence of an insert into delivery_status_events across the migrations is inside a SECURITY DEFINER function body, not a client-facing RLS policy.
questions.verify_output:
supabase/migrations/20260708000500_status_events_and_rpcs.sql: create policy "delivery_status_events_scoped_read" ...
supabase/migrations/20260708001000_fix_rls_recursion.sql: (same, recreated) -- both are SELECT policies only, no INSERT policy exists
questions.why_it_matters: An agent trying to log a status change with a plain client .insert() will get a silent RLS rejection or, worse, will 'fix' it by adding an insert policy that lets clients forge order history.

questions.question: In the order-lifecycle RPCs (e.g. accept_order), does the function check caller authorization in addition to the state-transition validity, given it runs as SECURITY DEFINER?
questions.ground_truth: Yes — e.g. accept_order explicitly checks has_restaurant_access(o.restaurant_id) before allowing the transition, on top of the status-guard exceptions.
questions.why_it_matters: SECURITY DEFINER bypasses RLS entirely; a new lifecycle RPC written by analogy without its own authorization check would let any authenticated user drive any order's state.

questions.question: When an RPC needs 'the current courier', does it resolve identity from the profiles table or from a separate couriers table?
questions.ground_truth: From couriers — RPCs look up `select id from public.couriers where user_id = auth.uid()`, never `profiles.role`.
questions.verify_cmd: grep -n 'from public.couriers where user_id = auth.uid' supabase/migrations/20260717001600_dispatch_offers.sql | head -3
questions.verify_output:
170:  select id into v_courier_id from public.couriers where user_id = auth.uid() and is_active;
211:  select id into v_courier_id from public.couriers where user_id = auth.uid() and is_active;
questions.why_it_matters: Checking only profiles.role='courier' without a matching couriers row silently treats a role-only account as a valid courier, or the reverse check fails and locks out real couriers.

questions.question: Once an order is inserted, can its delivery_fee_mdl column ever legitimately be changed by a later UPDATE?
questions.ground_truth: No — a BEFORE UPDATE trigger (guard_delivery_fee_floor) raises an exception on any change to delivery_fee_mdl once the row exists; it is write-once.
questions.why_it_matters: An agent trying to apply a retroactive fee correction via UPDATE will hit a hard DB exception instead of silently corrupting historical fee data (the trigger is the point).

questions.question: For a standard (non-catering) cash-on-delivery order, is there any total-amount cap enforced at checkout, and does that cap also apply to catering orders?
questions.ground_truth: Standard cash orders over 1400 MDL are rejected at place_order; catering orders are explicitly exempt from any cash cap.
questions.why_it_matters: Applying the 1400 MDL cash cap to catering orders (which routinely run into the thousands) would make catering permanently unbookable as cash; assuming no cap exists at all would reopen a dispatch dead-end that was deliberately fixed.

questions.question: Do the orders/order_items/catering_details money columns have database-level CHECK constraints preventing negative values, and is that true for every money column in the schema?
questions.ground_truth: Most money columns have `>= 0` CHECKs, but payouts.gross/net are deliberately excluded — a clawback net can be legitimately negative.
questions.verify_output:
alter table public.orders
  add constraint orders_subtotal_mdl_nonneg check (subtotal_mdl >= 0),
  add constraint orders_delivery_fee_mdl_nonneg check (delivery_fee_mdl >= 0),
... (payouts gross/net excluded per comment: 'a clawback net is legitimately negative')
questions.why_it_matters: Adding a blanket `>= 0` constraint to payouts would make legitimate clawback corrections fail at the database layer.

questions.question: How are corrections applied to versioned config tables like pricing_config, cash_policy, and courier_tariff_config — in-place UPDATE or a new row?
questions.ground_truth: A new row — these tables are append-only/immutable-history; the setter functions insert a new version rather than updating the current one.
questions.verify_output: 77:  insert into public.cash_policy (cap_mdl, reactivation_threshold_mdl, offload_channel_text,
questions.why_it_matters: UPDATEing a row in place would erase the version that pricing_config_at(ts) and other historical-lookup functions depend on for correctly billing past orders.

questions.question: After how many consecutive ignored (expired, un-responded) dispatch offers is a courier automatically set offline, and do explicit declines count toward that streak?
questions.ground_truth: 3 consecutive ignored/expired offers auto-offlines the courier; declines never increment the streak, only expiry does.
questions.verify_output:
43:    set consecutive_ignored_offers = consecutive_ignored_offers + 1
47:    if v_streak >= 3 then
questions.why_it_matters: Assuming declines count toward the ghost-offline streak would make an agent build a courier UI that discourages honest declines, which the design deliberately protects (declining is never penalized).

questions.question: Does the dispatch scoring function (dispatch_order) currently weight a courier's historical acceptance/decline rate at all, even at a low weight?
questions.ground_truth: No — the acceptance-rate term and its supporting lateral-join subquery were structurally removed from the function body, not just set to a zero weight.
questions.verify_output:
-- Fix is STRUCTURAL, not a zero-weighting: the (1 - acc.rate) * alpha1 term
-- and its supporting `acc` lateral-join subquery (which aggregated each
questions.why_it_matters: An agent that 'restores' the acceptance-rate term (e.g. while refactoring dispatch_order) would reintroduce reject-penalty scoring, which the migration comments tie to an EU legal constraint on dispatch fairness, not just a tuning preference.

questions.question: For an order with a future requested_for time, when does dispatch_order() actually start offering it to couriers relative to that time?
questions.ground_truth: Only once requested_for is within 45 minutes (dispatch_order returns null and holds every dispatch path until requested_for - 45min).
questions.verify_output: 75:  if v_order.requested_for is not null and v_order.requested_for > now() + interval '45 minutes' then
questions.why_it_matters: Assuming scheduled orders dispatch immediately (like ASAP orders) would make an agent 'fix' the apparent non-dispatch as a bug and remove a deliberate hold that prevents couriers picking up food far too early.

questions.question: In src/lib/realtime/subscribeTable.ts, is the channel name passed to supabase.channel() a fixed string or generated per call, and why does that matter?
questions.ground_truth: Generated per call as `${purpose}:${Date.now()}-${random}` — a static name breaks on React re-mounts ('cannot add postgres_changes callbacks after subscribe()').
questions.verify_output: 36:    const channelName = `${purpose}:${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`;
questions.why_it_matters: Reusing a static channel name across component re-mounts (a natural first instinct) throws at runtime and silently kills realtime updates on hot-reload/navigation.

questions.question: Is the courier's live-location broadcast channel (order:{id}:location) public or private, and does the client need to call anything besides subscribing?
questions.ground_truth: Private (`{config:{private:true}}`); the client must also call `supabase.realtime.setAuth()` to hand its JWT to the socket before it can send/receive on that channel.
questions.why_it_matters: Treating this channel as public (skipping setAuth or the private flag) either leaks a customer's live GPS trail to any subscriber or silently fails to deliver location updates to the intended parties.

questions.question: Do customer/courier/partner-facing postgres_changes subscriptions filter by row (e.g. id=eq.X), or do any of them subscribe to the whole table?
questions.ground_truth: Row-filtered — subscribeTable requires a `filter` argument for all callers except the admin ops surface, which is the one sanctioned whole-table case.
questions.why_it_matters: Omitting the row filter on a customer-facing subscription (copying the admin-ops pattern) would stream every other customer's order updates to that browser tab.

questions.question: What determines whether a given file in the restaurant-photos storage bucket is readable/writable by a given restaurant's staff — a metadata column, or something about the file path itself?
questions.ground_truth: The file path — storage RLS is path-scoped by the first path segment ({restaurantId}/...), which storage.foldername(name) extracts.
questions.why_it_matters: Uploading a menu photo under any path other than {restaurantId}/... (e.g. a flat filename) will pass the client-side compression step but then silently fail the storage RLS write policy.

questions.question: Does the private delivery-proof storage bucket have any UPDATE or DELETE policy for couriers, customers, or admins?
questions.ground_truth: No — only INSERT (assigned courier) and SELECT (order's customer + admin) policies exist; the absence of update/delete policies is itself the append-only enforcement (RLS default-deny).
questions.verify_output:
create policy "delivery_proof_courier_write" on storage.objects
  for insert to authenticated ...
create policy "delivery_proof_read" on storage.objects
  for select to authenticated ...
questions.why_it_matters: An agent asked to let a courier 'retake' a proof-of-delivery photo by updating the existing storage object will find there's no policy allowing it — the design intentionally requires a new object, not an overwrite.

questions.question: Is a proof-of-delivery photo (in the delivery-proof bucket) ever used as a gate on advance_delivery_status, or kept indefinitely?
questions.ground_truth: Never a gate (soft evidence only, no coupling to advance_delivery_status), and it is purged after 90 days by purge_expired_pii().
questions.verify_output: 125:  delete from storage.objects where bucket_id = 'delivery-proof' and created_at < now() - interval '90 days';
questions.why_it_matters: Building a delivery-confirmation flow that requires the photo before marking 'delivered' would block legitimate deliveries where the courier skips the optional photo; assuming it's retained forever misses a GDPR-driven purge job.

questions.question: Does `npm test` execute the SQL files under tests/rpc, or only the tests/unit suite?
questions.ground_truth: Only tests/unit — vitest.config.mts includes only `tests/unit/**/*.test.ts`; tests/rpc/*.sql is run by the separate `npm run test:rpc` script.
questions.why_it_matters: Reporting 'tests pass' after only `npm test` skips the entire RLS/RPC/money-invariant SQL suite, which is where most of this repo's actual behavioral guarantees are proven.

questions.question: What are the prerequisites for `npm run test:rpc` to run successfully, and what happens if they're not met?
questions.ground_truth: Requires a running Docker container named `supabase_db_chisinau-delivery`; if absent, the script prints SKIP and exits 1 without running tests.
questions.verify_output:
DB_CONTAINER="supabase_db_chisinau-delivery"
if ! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q "^${DB_CONTAINER}$"; then
  echo "SKIP: ${DB_CONTAINER} not running (supabase start first)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
questions.why_it_matters: An agent that runs test:rpc without `supabase start` first will get a nonzero exit and could misreport it as a real test failure rather than an unmet precondition.

questions.question: How does each tests/rpc/*.sql file signal a failing assertion to the test runner — a special test framework, or something else?
questions.ground_truth: The files are plain SQL wrapped in BEGIN/ROLLBACK; a failed assertion RAISEs a Postgres exception, which makes psql exit non-zero — there is no separate assertion framework.
questions.verify_output:
# RPC regression suite (audit #26/#27): every tests/rpc/*.sql file runs wrapped in
# BEGIN/ROLLBACK against the LOCAL Supabase db (superuser; auth simulated via
# request.jwt.claims). Tests self-assert: any FAIL raises an exception → non-zero
questions.why_it_matters: An agent adding a new RPC test who just prints 'FAIL: ...' without a RAISE EXCEPTION will get a test file that always reports success regardless of the actual assertion result.

questions.question: Can plain shell commands (e.g. `ls`, `npm test`) be assumed to work as-is on this machine's default shell, or is there a known quirk?
questions.ground_truth: There's a known quirk — plain commands can fail with `command not found: _lc`; commands need to be run wrapped in a clean env (e.g. `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=... bash -c '<cmd>'`).
questions.verify_output: WRAP=(env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin")
questions.why_it_matters: An agent hitting `command not found: _lc` on an unrelated command might assume the tool itself is missing/broken and go install/reconfigure things, instead of just wrapping the call.

questions.question: What local Postgres port does the Supabase CLI use for this project's local DB, per supabase/config.toml?
questions.ground_truth: 54422 (not the Supabase CLI's usual default of 54322).
questions.verify_output:
[db]
# Port to use for the local database URL.
port = 54422
questions.why_it_matters: An agent connecting with a hardcoded default port (54322) from Supabase docs/muscle memory will fail to reach this project's local database.

questions.question: In development (NODE_ENV !== 'production'), does the /master doorway require a username+password by default, or does something bypass that?
questions.ground_truth: It bypasses the password by default in dev — masterPasswordRequired() only returns true in production or when DISABLE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=1 is set; otherwise dev entry is passwordless.
questions.why_it_matters: An agent asked to 'test that the master password gate works' in local dev will find it doesn't prompt at all unless DISABLE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=1 is exported first, and might wrongly conclude the auth check is broken.

questions.question: If a developer edits NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL in .env.local while the Next.js dev server is already running, does the running app pick up the new value on the next request?
questions.ground_truth: No — NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables are inlined into the client bundle at build time, so the process needs a rebuild/restart to see the change, not just a page refresh.
questions.verify_output:
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=replace-with-local-anon-key-from-supabase-start-output
(server-only SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY listed separately below it)
questions.why_it_matters: An agent debugging a stale Supabase URL by only editing .env.local and refreshing the browser will keep seeing the old value and could misdiagnose it as a caching or code bug.

questions.question: Is the code under mobile/ included in the root project's TypeScript/ESLint checks (tsc --noEmit, eslint), or does it have its own toolchain?
questions.ground_truth: It has its own toolchain — both tsconfig.json and eslint.config.mjs explicitly exclude the mobile/ directory.
questions.verify_output:
tsconfig.json:  "exclude": ["node_modules", "mobile"]
eslint.config.mjs:    // Expo apps — own toolchain, not part of the Next.js build/lint.
eslint.config.mjs:    "mobile/**",
questions.why_it_matters: Running `npm run typecheck`/`npm run lint` at the root will never catch a TypeScript or lint error introduced inside mobile/client or mobile/driver, so 'checks pass' doesn't cover the mobile apps.

questions.question: How many separate Expo/React Native apps live under mobile/, and what does each one's package.json name it?
questions.ground_truth: 2 — mobile/client (package name "dragons-couriers-client") for customers, and mobile/driver (package name "dragons-couriers-driver") for couriers.
questions.verify_output:
mobile/client/package.json:2:  "name": "dragons-couriers-client",
mobile/driver/package.json:2:  "name": "dragons-couriers-driver",
questions.why_it_matters: Assuming there's a single unified mobile app (or that mobile/client serves couriers because of its package name) leads an agent to edit the wrong app for a given role's feature request.

questions.question: How many .sql files currently exist under supabase/migrations/?
questions.ground_truth: 98 files.
questions.why_it_matters: Documentation can lag a fast-moving migrations folder (an older doc snapshot cited 67); an agent trusting a stale count when auditing 'is every migration applied/documented' will undercount and miss recent ones.

questions.question: How many .sql files exist under tests/rpc/, and does that number equal the number of individual test assertions ('sims') in the suite?
questions.ground_truth: 66 files; not the same as the assertion count — most files contain multiple self-asserting sims/PASS lines, so file count is a lower bound on assertion count, not equal to it.
questions.why_it_matters: An agent asked to 'run all N sims' who equates file count with sim count will misreport coverage; and conflating this with the 23 tests/unit/*.test.ts files (a different suite, run by a different command) compounds the error.
